A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LumiNet. Their text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated training details and qualitative galleries.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIIW relighting experiments, geometry-consistency measurements, a 31-participant user study and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports corrected relighting results, decoder and seed-selection comparisons, data-generation ablations, and retained geometry and user-study results.

M1.justification: v3 adds a fine-tuned bypass decoder that replaces Stable Diffusion's default decoder during inference to preserve image details (Section 5.4). This is a localized architecture extension; the variational data-generation pipeline, latent ControlNet, lighting adaptor, losses and existing post-processing procedures remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIIW, BigTime, LSUN Bedroom and generated indoor scenes, with controlled and in-the-wild indoor relighting evaluations. Revised examples, decoder training and additional ablations remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The MIIW visual comparison expands from Latent-Intrinsic and RGB-X in v1 Figure 5 to include supervised/unsupervised SA-AE, S3Net-Depth and RGB↔X* in v3 Figure 4. Most comparator families already appeared quantitatively; the principal quantitative and user-study baseline sets remain.

E3.justification: v3 acknowledges an evaluation-code correction and specifies official Latent-Intrinsics evaluation with data range [-1,1]. It adds same-scene/ground-truth-irradiance RGB↔X conditions, decoder and seed-selection controls, and FID/CLIP-Score evaluation. Seed-selection use remains ambiguous: Section 5.5 excludes MIIW post-processing, but Table 1 distinguishes results without seed selection.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative decoder and seed-selection ablations in Table 1 and separates the effects of variational generation and CLIP filtering in Table 3. Figure 6 adds a same-scene, multiple-lighting demonstration. The earlier component ablation and 30-seed illustration remain, with the latter relocated to Figure S.1.

E5.justification: v1 Section 6.2 explicitly reports repeating MIIW experiments with different seeds and averaging results; v3 removes this statement. This is reduced reporting, not evidence that fewer runs occurred. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests, and the separate 30-seed selection illustration is retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially changes values and rankings. v1 reports raw RMSE/SSIM of 0.180/0.647 for Ours; v3 reports 0.343/0.359 for Ours (previous) and 0.310/0.440 for its final model, which no longer leads the benchmark. RGB↔X scores also change substantially. These reflect evaluation corrections and revised variants. Table 2 is numerically unchanged; Table 3 and revised qualitative outputs add results.

T1.justification: The relighting formulation and losses in Equations 1–3 remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. Revised conceptual grounding and decoder explanations do not constitute new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v3 removes v1's introductory claim of exceeding MIIW state of the art by over 20% and its concluding state-of-the-art characterization. Section 6.1 instead acknowledges trailing SA-AE and Latent-Intrinsic while outperforming RGB↔X. The framework, data-generation and cross-scene generalization contributions remain, but comparative success is materially narrowed.

C2.justification: v3 reframes benchmark performance around MIIW specialists versus broadly trained generalists and introduces pixel-metric sensitivity as an explanation for disagreement with visual quality. It explains the bypass decoder's identity-preservation role and adds discussion of long-range lighting failures. Existing limitations concerning small lamps, dramatic chromaticity, intensity control and missing ground truth largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents bypass-decoder fine-tuning on MIIW/BigTime with color jitter and additive noise, clarifies lighting-code rescaling and encoder freezing, and identifies the evaluation-code source. Core training hardware, optimizer, resolution, runtime and DDIM settings are retained in Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds relevant literature on compositing, ScribbleLight, Spotlight, perceptual lighting evaluation, bypass decoding and shadow-geometry failures, while removing the standalone NeRF reference. It also distinguishes specialist and generalist competitors. The central positioning as latent-intrinsic control combined with diffusion remains.

P1.justification: Related work, the overview, discussion and numerous captions are substantially condensed or rewritten. Post-processing moves into the method section, training details move into a formal supplement, and experimental subsections are reorganized. These changes materially alter the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: v3 rebuilds the MIIW comparison figure, revises the in-the-wild comparison, adds a multiple-lighting grid and Table 3, and restructures Table 1 by training regime with additional rows. Seed-search and gallery figures move into the supplement, with gallery imagery and crops also revised.

improvement.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges an evaluation-code bug, corrects Table 1 and withdraws the central claim of over 20% MIIW superiority, substantially improving evidential reliability. New decoder and data-generation ablations strengthen support. Inconsistent seed-selection wording and lost repeated-run reporting remain drawbacks, but they do not outweigh correction of the misleading benchmark conclusion and the added evidence.
